exercises.heading: Section 3.3 Exercises
exercises.paragraph: Find the arc length of the curve on the given interval.

problem.paragraph: $$\mathbf{ \text{r} }(t) = t^{2}\mathbf{ \text{i} } + 14t\mathbf{ \text{j} }, 0 \leq t \leq 7.$$ This portion of the graph is shown here:
$$\mathbf{ \text{r} }(t) = t^{2}\mathbf{ \text{i} } + (2t^{2} + 1)\mathbf{ \text{j} }, 1 \leq t \leq 3$$
$$\mathbf{ \text{r} }(t) = \left\langle {2\sin t,5t,2\cos t} \right\rangle,0 \leq t \leq \pi.$$ This portion of the graph is shown here:
$$\mathbf{ \text{r} }(t) = \left\langle {t^{2} + 1,4t^{3} + 3} \right\rangle, - 1 \leq t \leq 0$$

$$\mathbf{ \text{r} }(t) = \left\langle {e^{-t}\cos t,e^{-t}\sin t} \right\rangle$$ over the interval $$\left\lbrack {0,\frac{\pi}{2}} \right\rbrack.$$ Here is the portion of the graph on the indicated interval:
Find the length of one turn of the helix given by $$\mathbf{ \text{r} }(t) = \frac{1}{2}\cos t\mathbf{ \text{i} } + \frac{1}{2}\sin t\mathbf{ \text{j} } + \sqrt{\frac{3}{4}} t \mathbf{ \text{k} }.$$
Find the arc length of the vector-valued function $$\mathbf{ \text{r} }(t) = - t\mathbf{ \text{i} } + 4t\mathbf{ \text{j} } + 3t\mathbf{ \text{k} }$$ over $$\lbrack 0,1\rbrack.$$

A particle travels once around a circle with the equation of motion $$\mathbf{ \text{r} }(t) = 3\cos t\mathbf{ \text{i} } + 3\sin t\mathbf{ \text{j} } + 0\mathbf{ \text{k} }.$$ Find the distance traveled around the circle by the particle.
Set up an integral to find the circumference of the ellipse with the equation $$\mathbf{ \text{r} }(t) = \cos t\mathbf{ \text{i} } + 2\sin t\mathbf{ \text{j} } + 0\mathbf{ \text{k} }.$$
Find the length of the curve $$\mathbf{ \text{r} }(t) = \left\langle {\sqrt{2}t,e^{t},e^{-t}} \right\rangle$$ over the interval $$0 \leq t \leq 1.$$ The graph is shown here:
Find the length of the curve $$\mathbf{ \text{r} }(t) = \left\langle {2\sin t,5t,2\cos t} \right\rangle$$ for $$t \in \left\lbrack {-10,10} \right\rbrack.$$

The position function for a particle is $$\mathbf{ \text{r} }(t) = a\cos (\omega t)\mathbf{ \text{i} } + b\sin (\omega t)\mathbf{ \text{j} }.$$ Find the unit tangent vector and the unit normal vector at $$t = 0.$$
Given $$\mathbf{ \text{r} }(t) = a\cos (\omega t)\mathbf{ \text{i} } + b\sin (\omega t)\mathbf{ \text{j} },$$ find the binormal vector $$\mathbf{ \text{B} }(0).$$
Given $$\mathbf{ \text{r} }(t) = \left\langle {2e^{t},e^{t}\cos t,e^{t}\sin t} \right\rangle,$$ determine the tangent vector $$\mathbf{ \text{T} }(t).$$
Given $$\mathbf{ \text{r} }(t) = \left\langle {2e^{t},e^{t}\cos t,e^{t}\sin t} \right\rangle,$$ determine the unit tangent vector $$\mathbf{ \text{T} }(t)$$ evaluated at $$t = 0.$$

Given $$\mathbf{ \text{r} }(t) = \left\langle {2e^{t},e^{t}\cos t,e^{t}\sin t} \right\rangle,$$ find the unit normal vector $$\mathbf{ \text{N} }(t)$$ evaluated at $$t = 0,$$ $$\mathbf{ \text{N} }(0).$$
Given $$\mathbf{ \text{r} }(t) = \left\langle {2e^{t},e^{t}\cos t,e^{t}\sin t} \right\rangle,$$ find the unit binormal vector evaluated at $$t = 0.$$
Given $$\mathbf{ \text{r} }(t) = t\mathbf{ \text{i} } + t^{2}\mathbf{ \text{j} } + t\mathbf{ \text{k} },$$ find the unit tangent vector $$\mathbf{ \text{T} }(t).$$ The graph is shown here:

Find the unit tangent vector $$\mathbf{ \text{T} }(t)$$ and unit normal vector $$\mathbf{ \text{N} }(t)$$ at $$t = 0$$ for the plane curve $$\mathbf{ \text{r} }(t) = \left\langle {t^{3} - 4t,5t^{2} - 2} \right\rangle.$$ The graph is shown here:
Find the unit tangent vector $$\mathbf{ \text{T} }(t)$$ for $$\mathbf{ \text{r} }(t) = 3t\mathbf{ \text{i} } + 5t^{2}\mathbf{ \text{j} } + 2t\mathbf{ \text{k} }$$
Find the principal normal vector to the curve $$\mathbf{ \text{r} }(t) = \left\langle {6\cos t,6\sin t} \right\rangle$$ at the point determined by $$t = {\pi/3}.$$
Find $$\mathbf{ \text{T} }(t)$$ for the curve $$\mathbf{ \text{r} }(t) = \left( {t^{3} - 4t} \right)\mathbf{ \text{i} } + \left( {5t^{2} - 2} \right)\mathbf{ \text{j} }.$$
Find $$\mathbf{ \text{N} }(t)$$ for the curve $$\mathbf{ \text{r} }(t) = \left( {t^{3} - 4t} \right)\mathbf{ \text{i} } + \left( {5t^{2} - 2} \right)\mathbf{ \text{j} }.$$
Find the unit normal vector $$\mathbf{ \text{N} }(t)$$ for $$\mathbf{ \text{r} }(t) = \left\langle {2\sin t,5t,2\cos t} \right\rangle.$$

solution.paragraph: $$N ( t ) = 〈 - sin t , 0 , - cos t 〉 N ( t ) = 〈 - sin t , 0 , - cos t 〉$$

problem.paragraph: Find the unit tangent vector $$\mathbf{ \text{T} }(t)$$ for $$\mathbf{ \text{r} }(t) = \left\langle {2\sin t,5t,2\cos t} \right\rangle.$$
Find the arc-length function $$s(t)$$ for the line segment given by $$\mathbf{ \text{r} }(t) = \left\langle {3 - 3t,4t} \right\rangle.$$ Write r as a parameter of s.

solution.paragraph: Arc-length function: $$s(t)=5t;s(t)=5t;$$ r as a parameter of s: $$r(s)=(3-3s5)i+4s5jr(s)=(3-3s5)i+4s5j$$

problem.paragraph: Parameterize the helix $$\mathbf{ \text{r} }(t) = \cos t\mathbf{ \text{i} } + \sin t\mathbf{ \text{j} } + t\mathbf{ \text{k} }$$ using the arc-length parameter s, from $$t = 0.$$
Parameterize the curve using the arc-length parameter s, at the point at which $$t = 0$$ for $$\mathbf{ \text{r} }(t) = e^{t}\sin t\mathbf{ \text{i} } + e^{t}\cos t\mathbf{ \text{j} }.$$
Find the curvature of the curve $$\mathbf{ \text{r} }(t) = 5\cos t\mathbf{ \text{i} } + 4\sin t\mathbf{ \text{j} }$$ at $$t = {\pi/3}.$$ (Note: The graph is an ellipse.)
Find the x-coordinate at which the curvature of the curve $$y = {1/x}$$ is a maximum value.

solution.paragraph: The maximum value of the curvature occurs at $$x=1.x=1.$$

problem.paragraph: Find the curvature of the curve $$\mathbf{ \text{r} }(t) = 5\cos t\mathbf{ \text{i} } + 5\sin t\mathbf{ \text{j} }.$$ Does the curvature depend upon the parameter t?
Find the curvature $$\kappa$$ for the curve $$y = x - \frac{1}{4}x^{2}$$ at the point $$x = 2.$$
Find the curvature $$\kappa$$ for the curve $$y = \frac{1}{3}x^{3}$$ at the point $$x = 1.$$
Find the curvature $$\kappa$$ of the curve $$\mathbf{ \text{r} }(t) = t\mathbf{ \text{i} } + 6t^{2}\mathbf{ \text{j} } + 4t\mathbf{ \text{k} }.$$ The graph is shown here:
Find the curvature of $$\mathbf{ \text{r} }(t) = \left\langle {2\sin t,5t,2\cos t} \right\rangle.$$
Find the curvature of $$\mathbf{ \text{r} }(t) = \sqrt{2}t\mathbf{ \text{i} } + e^{t}\mathbf{ \text{j} } + e^{-t}\mathbf{ \text{k} }$$ at point $$P\left( {0,1,1} \right).$$
At what point does the curve $$y = e^{x}$$ have maximum curvature?
What happens to the curvature as $$x\rightarrow\infty$$ for the curve $$y = e^{x}?$$
Find the point of maximum curvature on the curve $$y = \ln x.$$
Find the equations of the normal plane and the osculating plane of the curve $$\mathbf{ \text{r} }(t) = \left\langle {2\sin (3t),t,2\cos (3t)} \right\rangle$$ at point $$\left( {0,\pi,-2} \right).$$
Find equations of the osculating circles of the ellipse $$4y^{2} + 9x^{2} = 36$$ at the points $$(2,0)$$ and $$(0,3).$$
Find the equation for the osculating plane at point $$t = {\pi/4}$$ on the curve $$\mathbf{ \text{r} }(t) = \cos (2t)\mathbf{ \text{i} } + \sin (2t)\mathbf{ \text{j} } + t\mathbf{ \text{k} }.$$
Find the radius of curvature of $$6y = x^{3}$$ at the point $$\left( {2,\frac{4}{3}} \right).$$
Find the curvature at each point $$\left( {x,y} \right)$$ on the hyperbola $$\mathbf{ \text{r} }(t) = \left\langle {a\cosh (t),b\sinh (t)} \right\rangle.$$
Calculate the curvature of the circular helix $$\mathbf{ \text{r} }(t) = r\sin (t)\mathbf{ \text{i} } + r\cos (t)\mathbf{ \text{j} } + t\mathbf{ \text{k} }.$$
Find the radius of curvature of $$y = \ln (x + 1)$$ at point $$\left( {2,\ln 3} \right).$$
Find the radius of curvature of the hyperbola $$xy = 1$$ at point $$(1,1).$$

exercises.paragraph: A particle moves along the plane curve C described by $$\mathbf{ \text{r} }(t) = t\mathbf{ \text{i} } + t^{2}\mathbf{ \text{j} }.$$ Solve the following problems.

problem.paragraph: Find the length of the curve over the interval $$\left\lbrack {0,2} \right\rbrack.$$
Find the curvature of the plane curve at $$t = 0,1,2.$$
Describe the curvature as t increases from $$t = 0$$ to $$t = 2.$$

solution.paragraph: The curvature is decreasing over this interval.

problem.paragraph: [T] Use technology to graph the surface.
